observations: Red and black motorcycle with 'BOXER' written on the fuel tank in photo 0, 1, and 2.
The engine casing has 'BAJAJ' visible in photo 0.
The motorcycle has a single black seat, chrome exhaust, and front and rear fenders.
Front wheel has a disc brake, rear wheel has a drum brake.
The handlebars have black grips and a headlight with turn signals.
The fuel tank has visible scratches and wear, especially around the 'BOXER' logo.
The seat appears worn and slightly torn in photo 1.
The front fender is chipped and has paint damage in photo 2.
The motorcycle is parked on dirt ground, with no visible license plate or registration.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JUMIA MARKETGROUP' is present on all photos.

claims.claim: Send new BAJAJ ready to be sold out to the first lucky customer.
claims.evidence: The motorcycle shows significant wear and tear: scratches on the fuel tank, chipped front fender, worn seat, and dirt on the body. These indicate use, contradicting the claim of being 'new'.

risks.risk: The motorcycle may not start or run properly due to unseen mechanical issues.
risks.proof: A video showing the engine starting and running smoothly, with no unusual noises or smoke.

risks.risk: The motorcycle may have a damaged or non-functional electrical system (e.g., lights, horn, indicators).
risks.proof: A video showing all lights, horn, and indicators functioning.

risks.risk: The motorcycle may have a history of accidents or structural damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the frame and swingarm for cracks or bends.

risks.risk: The motorcycle may be stolen or have a compromised title/registration.
risks.proof: Photo of the vehicle's VIN plate and a copy of the title or registration document.

proof_requests: Video of the motorcycle starting and running.
Video of all lights, horn, and indicators working.
Close-up photo of the frame and swingarm for damage.
Photo of the VIN plate and title/registration document.
response.reason: The motorcycle is identified as a Bajaj Boxer, but the seller's claim of it being 'new' is contradicted by visible wear and tear. Key functional and ownership risks cannot be assessed from the photos alone, so proof is required before pricing.
